headline: Markets Brace for Two More Fed Rate Hikes in 2026
summary: As of late September 2026, markets were pricing in two additional 25 basis point Federal Reserve rate hikes for the remainder of 2026, which would take the fed funds target to 4.25-4.50%. The first September hike raised the rate to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike in more than three years, driven by energy-related inflation from the Middle East conflict.
key_facts: Market prices in 2 more hikes for 2026 (as of late Sept)
September hike raised rate to 3.75-4.00% (first in 3+ years)
Hikes driven by Middle East energy-inflation shock
Year-end target ~4.25-4.50% if two hikes proceed
Energy prices from Iran conflict primary inflation driver

headline: Fed Hikes 25 Bps in 12-0 Vote, Commits to Inflation Fight
summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 12-0 in September 2026 to raise the fed funds target by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, the first rate increase in more than three years. The Fed committed to continuing the inflation fight, citing energy-driven price pressures linked to the Iran conflict as the key concern.
key_facts: FOMC voted 12-0 to hike 25 bps in September 2026
Energy-driven inflation (Iran conflict) cited as key concern
